problem: Existing fact-checking solutions typically require active engagement, such as searching for questionable claims, which disrupts natural conversations and real-time interactions (p.1). Fact-checking in real-time is inherently inconvenient, socially awkward, and prone to being forgotten (p.1).
methodology: The authors present Factually, a wearable live fact-checking system that integrates with everyday wearable devices like smartwatches or rings to provide real-time, discreet feedback through vibrations when potentially false information is detected (p.1). The proof-of-concept system consists of a wearable interface, a fact-checking backend leveraging large language models and web-based resources, and a real-time processing pipeline that transcribes and analyzes audio input for potentially false claims (p.4).
results: Initial qualitative feedback from 10 potential users showed that participants found Factually intuitive and useful, particularly appreciating its non-intrusive nature and expressing interest in daily use (p.5). Users suggested improvements regarding the specificity of the vibrotactile feedback and the ability to customize system sensitivity to different topics (p.5).
key_findings: Factually demonstrates the potential to extend human perceptual capabilities by identifying incorrect statements and providing accurate information in real time during health, social, and everyday learning scenarios (p.4, p.5). Its subtle design and tactile feedback support seamless integration into social interactions while promoting introspection, self-correction, and critical thinking (p.4, p.5).
limitations: The current prototype employs general-purpose large language models and web-based resources that may not always produce domain-specific or highly accurate results (p.5). Cloud-based fact-checking introduces network latency that can delay real-time feedback, and broader long-term usability studies are needed to assess practicality, social acceptability, cognitive load, and ethical implications like privacy (p.5-6).
title: Factually: Exploring Wearable Fact-Checking for Augmented Truth Discernment
